notes: SOURCE: all six panels are vector graphics (page 19 bottom: Fig. 17; page 21 left column: Figs. 21 and 22). Every curve is stored as ONE filled polygon that is the outline of the stroked line (stroke-to-path conversion by the typesetter); tick labels are also outlined glyphs, so page.get_text('dict') returns no tick-label text for these figures.

AXIS CALIBRATION: tick positions are the centres of the tick-mark rectangles found in page.get_drawings(); tick values (e.g. 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0) were read from the rendered page and confirmed in the overlay PNGs (green labels drawn at each tick mark coincide with the printed labels). Linear least-squares map with 4-9 ticks per axis; max residual < 2e-4 data units on every axis.

CENTRELINE RECOVERY: each outline polygon was split at its min-x and max-x vertices into the two stroke sides; every vertex on one side was paired with the nearest point of the other side (point-to-segment projection) and the midpoint taken; pairs whose separation differs from the stroke width by >40% (end caps) were dropped. Stroke width: 1.05 pt (Fig. 17), 0.71 pt (Figs. 21-22). A second, independent method (averaging the two sides at equal x) was used to estimate extraction uncertainty ('derived_statistics_extraction_uncertainty' = |difference| between the two methods).

HOW THE STATISTICS WERE OBTAINED (NOT tabulated in the paper): for PDF curves the piecewise-linear centreline was densified (dx = 2e-4, exact for a polyline), negative values (baseline offsets <= 0.004) clipped to 0, the area computed by the trapezoidal rule ('raw_area') and the curve divided by it; then mean = int x f dx, std = sqrt(int (x-mean)^2 f dx), median = x where the cumulative integral = 0.5, mode = vertex of a parabola fitted to the points within 2% of the peak, P(X<1) = cumulative integral at x = 1. For CDF curves the centreline was made monotone (running maximum) and clipped to [0,1]; median = x where F = 0.5 (linear interpolation), P(X<1) = F(1). mean/std 'crosscheck' from the CDF use mean = x0 + int (1-F) dx and E[X^2] = x0^2 + int 2x(1-F) dx over the drawn support (tail beyond the last drawn point ignored).

HIDDEN DATA INCLUDED: several curves extend beyond the visible axes in the vector data (hidden by the axes clip path) - e.g. Fig. 17 PDF of Gamma up to 2.775 (visible xlim 0.5-2.26), Fig. 17 CDF of F_s from 0.015 to 2.158, Fig. 21 PDF of Gamma up to 6.485 (visible 0-6), Fig. 22 CDF of F_s up to 2.229, Fig. 22 CDF of Gamma up to 8.045. These hidden parts were kept and used for the statistics; each series lists them in 'hidden_parts'.

TRUNCATION: the Fig. 21 PDF of Gamma ends at Gamma = 6.485 with density still ~0.003-0.007 and the Fig. 22 CDF of Gamma reaches only F = 0.9967 at Gamma = 8.045; the long upper tail of Gamma (Example 5.3.2) is therefore cut, and the mean and especially the std of Gamma are biased low: PDF-based mean/std 1.866/0.823 vs CDF-based 1.905/0.939. Treat std(Gamma) for Example 5.3.2 as uncertain by ~+-0.1. Fig. 17 curves decay fully to zero, so their moments are reliable (mean to ~0.002, std to ~0.004).

RESOLUTION: the Fig. 21 PDF of Gamma is drawn with vertices only every ~0.094 in Gamma (coarse KDE grid), so its mode (1.43) is uncertain by about +-0.05; all other curves are dense (vertex spacing <= 0.03).

CONSISTENCY CHECKS against the paper text: P(X<1) from the curves vs the failure probabilities quoted in the text - Example 5.3.1 Gamma: 6.61% (PDF) / 6.46% (CDF) vs Pf = 6.5% (text); Cho F_s: 7.55% (PDF) / 7.61% (CDF) vs 7.9%. Example 5.3.2 Gamma: 6.62% (PDF) / 5.52% (CDF) vs Pf = 5.50%; Cho F_s: 6.20% (PDF) / 5.15% (CDF) vs 6.37%. KDE smoothing of the PDFs spreads mass into the lower tail, so for Pf the CDF readings are preferable (they reproduce the quoted LA values).

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY (Example 5.3.2, Cho F_s): the red PDF of Fig. 21 (raw area 1.029, i.e. not a normalised density) and the red CDF of Fig. 22 do not describe the same distribution: integrating the PDF gives a CDF that differs from the plotted CDF by up to 0.028 (at F_s ~ 1.13), std 0.153 vs 0.139, P(F_s<1) 6.2% vs 5.15%. For Example 5.3.1 the PDF-integrated and plotted CDFs agree within 0.009 (F_s) and 0.0024 (Gamma). For Gamma in 5.3.2 they differ by up to 0.012 near Gamma = 1 (KDE smoothing).

NOTE on axes: Figure 21 right (PDF of Gamma) has x 0..6 while Figure 22 right (CDF of Gamma) has x 0..8; Figure 21 left (PDF of F_s) has x 0..3 and Figure 22 left (CDF of F_s) x 0..2. Gamma and F_s are not numerically comparable for phi != 0 (paper Section 4.2), only P(.<1) is.
